blocks.content:
Connect a Kubernetes cluster to Grafana Cloud using the Kubernetes Monitoring Helm chart. You will configure collection in Grafana, run the generated command in your terminal, and check that data arrives.

Before you start, you need permission to configure Kubernetes Monitoring, a Kubernetes cluster you can deploy to, and Helm and kubectl configured for that cluster.
Open the Kubernetes Monitoring setup wizard.
Open **Kubernetes > Configuration** to start the cluster setup wizard.
The wizard guides you through authentication, collection settings, and deployment.
Install or update the required rules, then select your Kubernetes platform.

whenTrue.content: Select **Do it** to install the alert rules and recording rules required by Kubernetes Monitoring. Wait for the installation to finish.
whenTrue.tooltip: Installs the required rules on this Grafana stack.

whenTrue.content: Select **Do it** to upgrade the installed rules to the latest available backend version. Wait for the update to finish.
whenTrue.tooltip: Updates the rules to the available version.

whenFalse.content: The alert rules and recording rules are installed. If no upgrade is offered, continue with the current version.
whenFalse.tooltip: Confirms that the required rules are installed.

blocks.tooltip: Choose the platform that matches your cluster.
blocks.content: Select the platform your cluster runs on. **Do it** selects **Kubernetes** for EKS on EC2, standard GKE, or a self-managed cluster. For AKS, GKE Autopilot, EKS on Fargate, IBM Cloud, or OpenShift, select the matching card yourself.
Once the rules are installed and any available upgrade has finished, select **Next** to configure authentication.
The backend rules support Kubernetes Monitoring, and the platform selection determines the available collectors.
Configure the credential that Alloy will use to send telemetry to Grafana Cloud.

blocks.tooltip: Use a descriptive name for this credential.
blocks.content:
Name the token so you can identify its cluster or purpose later. **Do it** enters `k8s-monitoring-alloy`; replace it if needed.

If you already have a suitable token, select **Use an existing token**, enter it yourself, and skip the token-creation steps.

blocks.tooltip: Review the access this credential will grant.
blocks.content: Review the predefined scopes. They allow Alloy to send telemetry and the wizard to read metrics for its connection check.

blocks.tooltip: Create and securely save your credential.
blocks.content: Select **Create token** yourself, then store the generated token securely. The wizard includes it in the generated deployment configuration.
Once the token is available, select **Next** to choose a deployment size.
The wizard uses this credential when generating the deployment configuration.
Choose the Alloy deployment size for your cluster.

blocks.tooltip: Select a deployment size for your cluster.
blocks.content: Select **Standard** for a balanced deployment. **Do it** selects this option. **Lightweight** reduces resource use for smaller clusters; **Scalable** separates collection across Alloy deployments. Select either alternative yourself if it better fits your cluster.

blocks.tooltip: Review how the deployment options differ.
blocks.content: Open the explanation to review the **Standard** deployment before continuing.
Select **Next** to choose which telemetry to collect.
The deployment size determines how collection workloads run in your cluster.
Review the telemetry you want to collect.

blocks.tooltip: Review the cluster telemetry to be collected.
blocks.content: Review **Kubernetes monitoring**, which collects the cluster metrics, events, and logs used by the app. Use its options menu to inspect individual collectors.

blocks.tooltip: Choose whether to create a managed service discovery pipeline.
blocks.content: Review **Auto-discover services**. Enable it to create a managed discovery pipeline in Fleet Management. Discovery does not collect application telemetry unless you also enable instrumentation.
Select **Next** after reviewing your collection settings.
Your collection settings determine which telemetry Alloy sends to Grafana Cloud.
Name the cluster, deploy the generated configuration, and test the connection.
Enter a unique cluster name that your team recognizes. This name identifies the cluster in Grafana; `production-eu-west` is an example, not a value to copy unchanged.
blocks.formHint: An example — replace it with your own

blocks.content: Choose the Kubernetes namespace for the Alloy deployment. **Do it** enters `monitoring`; use your team’s namespace if different. This does not limit monitoring to that namespace.

blocks.tooltip: Copy the command for your selected configuration.
blocks.content: Copy the generated Helm command. In your terminal, check `kubectl config current-context`, then run the command against the intended cluster. The command contains your access token, so keep it private.

blocks.tooltip: Apply the monitoring configuration and check the connection.
blocks.content: After the Helm command finishes and the collector pods start, select **Do it** to apply your monitoring configuration through Fleet Management and test the connection. Wait for the result; if it fails, check the deployment and credentials before retrying.
The connection check applies your monitoring configuration and checks the deployment; review its result before checking incoming metrics.
Check that the expected cluster metrics are arriving.
Open **Metrics status** to inspect which collectors are sending data.

blocks.tooltip: Check for data from the expected collectors.
blocks.content: Check the status for the cluster you configured and the collectors you enabled. Missing data needs investigation: confirm that the pods are running, their credentials are valid, and they can reach Grafana Cloud.
Once your cluster and its expected collectors report data, explore its nodes, workloads, and resource usage.
